facts: Sisir recalls receiving payment for story discussions without screen credit.

He recalls screenplay and dialogue discussions at his Jhanjiri Mangala home. Assistants Srikant Choudhury and Jyoti Nayak introduced Hara Patnaik as a theatre actor; he remembers them arriving on three bicycles.
sources.usable_paragraph: In Sisir Mishra’s recollection, screenplay and dialogue discussions took place at his home in Jhanjiri Mangala. Two assistants, Srikant Choudhury and Jyoti Nayak, brought along a theatre actor, Hara Patnaik. He remembered the three arriving on bicycles. The memory makes apprenticeship tangible: people coming together to work through a scene and its words.
limits: Do not infer introductions caused success or every attendee had equal opportunity.
Do not reuse unrelated problematic chronology, honorifics, film totals or planned Konark film.
Bheegi Palkein wife-source-story claim is interviewer framing, not confirmed original credits.

facts: Mishra recalls Shyamal Mukherjee teaching screenplay writing during Jajabara.

sources.usable_paragraph: Bijay Mishra’s account adds a writer’s apprenticeship: Shyamal Mukherjee taught him screenplay writing during Jajabara. He also described failures as occasions to examine his choices. Experience, in this telling, did not remove the need to learn.
limits: Screenplay anecdote already in Literature and Screen; keep brief or link.

sources.kind: Bijay Mandal retrospective with named participants quoted
facts: Actor Jayaswami says working with Mahapatra helped her evolve and that he kept actors within their characters.
Susant Mani remembers Mahapatra looking closely at learners’ rushes and guiding them.
Pradeep Mohanty recalls borrowing his35mm camera to avoid rental from Madras.
sources.usable_paragraph: Actor Jayaswami remembered developing through work with Manmohan Mahapatra, who kept performers close to their characters. Susant Mani described another kind of attention: watching learners’ rushes and offering guidance. These are accounts of learning through work already made, with someone willing to look at it carefully.
limits: Jayaswami is woman’s own quoted recollection; do not claim she speaks for all performers.
All three accounts already appear briefly in Manmohan profile; select new emphasis rather than repeat whole paragraph.
Same source also used in television chapter; no new award totals/firsts/release chronology.

limits: Sound training and childhood music teacher already in Searching for Sita Bibaha.

source_budget_policy: Max200 source-derived words per source across current public collection, including factual notes. Proposed allocations above are conservative new caps, not permission to ignore existing passages; final writer/reviewer must aggregate. No quotations required. MyCityLinks sources have no matching current Markdown source links in checked KB; other four are reused. Manmohan source is shared with television; Darai with Sita; Bijay with literature; Nirad with his profile.
narrative_recommendation: Use4–6 distinct short accounts, not six biographies. Open attributed Sisir home-discussion memory; Chandi connects theatre/assistant work; Bijay gives change in writing craft; Jayaswami/Susant give watching and feedback; Darai moves to sound and ongoing participation; Nirad can be a concise reading link. End with original questions about how to share time, attention and access, framed as possibilities not evidence of absent institutions.
do_not_add: No recreated scene or present-tense witness claim.
No universal apprenticeship pipeline or linear theatre-to-film evolution.
No equation of mentorship with obedience or uncredited labour being desirable.
No formal credit for unnamed/informal help without credits evidence.
No implication this small set represents all women, technicians or routes into cinema.
new_finding: The fresh Darai page supplies current self-described film-society volunteering and documentary mentorship alongside her training; Jayaswami’s own attributed words supply an actor perspective without relying on a husband’s account.
title: Learning Cinema Together evidence and limitations
editorial_decisions: Participant recollections attributed; no invented scene or anecdote ownership claim.
Darai identified as a mentor, not a recipient of Docustan mentorship.
Formal credits distinct from informal creative help acknowledged by Chandi.
No broad industry critique or claim that anecdotes represent all routes into filmmaking.
The new article links existing biographies rather than duplicating whole lives.
